title: Contaminated event window: confounding news during event period

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Cross-sectional multivariate event-study regression (sometimes called “conditional market model”).  
Idea: Every firm announces an acquisition on day 0, but the size of its earnings surprise (eps_surprise) differs.  
Step 1 – abnormal return:   AR_it = ret_it – β_i · mkt_ret_t  
Step 2 – cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over a short window W (e.g. –1..+1).  
Step 3 – decompose CAR_i with  
 CAR_i = α (acquisition effect) + θ · eps_surprise_i (earnings effect) + ε_i  

Key assumptions  
• Heterogeneity: the acquisition effect α is common across firms; variation in CAR comes from different earnings surprises.  
• No other news correlated with eps_surprise across firms during the window.  
• eps_surprise is measured without error (or errors are classical).  
Under these, α consistently estimates the pure acquisition reaction.

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
## Isolating acquisition effect from confounding earnings news
## Data: experiments/exp_b/data/s18_data.csv
############################################################

# 0) Libraries ---------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lmtest)      # for coeftest
  library(sandwich)    # for robust vcov
})

# 1) Read data ---------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s18_data.csv",
                col_types = cols())

# Quick check that eps_surprise exists; if not, stop.
if(!("eps_surprise" %in% names(dat))){
  stop("Column `eps_surprise` is not in the data. Analysis cannot proceed.")
}

# 2) Abnormal return ---------------------------------------------------------
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# 3) Function: run cross-sectional CAR regression ----------------------------
run_car_reg <- function(w_start, w_end){
  
  car_tab <- dat %>% 
    filter(event_day >= w_start & event_day <= w_end) %>% 
    group_by(stock_id) %>% 
    summarise(CAR = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE),
              eps_surprise = first(eps_surprise),
              .groups = "drop")
  
  fit <- lm(CAR ~ eps_surprise, data = car_tab)
  rob  <- coeftest(fit, vcov = vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1"))
  
  list(car_tab = car_tab,
       fit = fit,
       rob = rob)
}

# 4) Baseline window (-1, +1) -----------------------------------------------
base <- run_car_reg(-1, 1)

cat("\n=== Baseline window (-1, +1) ===\n")
print(base$rob)

acq_effect <- base$rob["(Intercept)", "Estimate"]
earn_coef  <- base$rob["eps_surprise", "Estimate"]
cat(sprintf("\nEstimated acquisition effect (CAR, -1..+1): %.4f\n", acq_effect))
cat(sprintf("Earnings-surprise coefficient:               %.4f\n", earn_coef))

# 5) Robustness checks -------------------------------------------------------

# (a) Single-day (0) reaction
day0 <- run_car_reg(0, 0)
cat("\n--- Robustness: Day 0 only ---\n")
print(day0$rob)

# (b) Wider window (-2, +2)
wide <- run_car_reg(-2, 2)
cat("\n--- Robustness: Window (-2, +2) ---\n")
print(wide$rob)

# 6) Clean numerical summary -------------------------------------------------
res <- data.frame(Window = c("[-1,1]", "[0,0]", "[-2,2]"),
                  Acquisition_Effect = c(acq_effect,
                                          day0$rob["(Intercept)", "Estimate"],
                                          wide$rob["(Intercept)", "Estimate"]))
cat("\n=== Numerical summary (acquisition CAR) ===\n")
print(res, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
• Sign: Positive. Both acquisitions and earnings beats are typically value-enhancing; after purging the earnings component, the remaining (acquisition) CAR should still be > 0.  
• Magnitude: For a –1..+1 window, I expect an acquisition CAR of roughly +1 % to +2 % (0.010–0.020). Earnings-surprise coefficient should be positive, perhaps ~0.25–0.35 (i.e., a 4 % EPS beat raises CAR by another 1 %).  
Rationale: Prior literature finds average acquisition announcements move prices by 1–2 % for non-diversifying deals, while quarterly earnings surprises of one cent typically shift returns ~3–5 %.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with confound adjustment — regress AR on eps_surprise + acquisition dummy
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: After controlling for earnings surprise, acquisition announcement generates negative AR
